findings.detail: organism ids[1]=2ca4d2ca0501 placed with no bespoke editing; identity gate held
blob_hash (content) identical across worlds; artifact_id (envelope) distinct — no identity collision

SFE accepts arbitrary bytes (content-addressed); it does NOT verify Proteus identity. Integrity is a CLIENT-side assertion (blob_hash==sha256:oid). An adapter that skips the gate would fossilize corrupted material with a wrong-but-valid blob_hash.
same seed_root=424242 thrice -> 3 distinct world_ids; config is NOT the identity (a replicate is a new world)
artifact write AFTER terminate SUCCEEDED — TERMINATED does not end write lifetime; matches the addendum caution
2nd experiment under limit=1 -> 409 (budget cap enforced at commit)
observation with no work_id -> engine_attested=0 (evidence_class CLIENT_ASSERTED). Nothing forces attestation; an agent can silently produce unattested 'evidence'.
GET .../events return shape is INCONSISTENT: dict {'events':[...]} in the first integration, bare list here. A client must defensively handle both or break (this harness did, mid-run).

PEW validates sfe_entry_hash SHAPE + (event_id,entry_hash) pair EXISTENCE in SFE, not that the event is the run's observation. Anchoring on WORLD_CREATED (evt evt_f1110bdb) would pass PEW shape checks — causal correctness is a CLIENT obligation, not enforced.
artifact retry with same idem_key -> same artifact_id (idempotent)
create_world has no idempotency key; a retried create mints a NEW world (see B1). An orchestrator that retries world creation on a timeout silently doubles worlds. UNSAFE-TO-RETRY-BLINDLY.
two worker identities claim work in two isolated worlds; work_id/claim_id separated
GET /v2/worlds returns a listing (n=189); an agent can enumerate worlds without shell archaeology
GET /packets -> 405 (source packets not independently readable over HTTP — archaeology gap, per note 7)
